blocks.rationale: Evidence and listening pass, but the edge falls before 19a: after the prior accusers’ charges and before “Well, then…19a,” displacing commentary anchored at 19b–19c.
Accurately orients the unit's oracle, examinations, and human-wisdom conclusion; the interruption is concise and lands between complete sentences before Chaerephon's account.
The claims are supported, but this is bare recap of the politician episode and overlaps the section's summary; before is the oracle-wide investigation, after begins its results.
Evidence fails: “jurors” is not established by the printed passage or cited records. Placement passes: edge follows “vehement slanders” and precedes “From among them Meletus...”.
The synthesis is accurate and listenable, but the edge follows “desert my post...” and precedes “It would be a terrible thing...,” displacing the 28b anchor into 29a.
The title’s “Arginusae” identification lacks matching printed or accepted support; the body is otherwise anchored and concise. Before: private-life conclusion; after: promised deeds.
The comparison and interpretive caution are supported and clear aloud. Before: Socrates answers the public-life question; after: he resumes his lifelong-consistency claim.
Grounded synthesis of the penalty sequence and examined life; the edge follows the silence challenge and precedes Socrates’ explanation, preserving the dramatic progression.
The argument is supported, but the edge follows the prytaneum exchange and precedes its proposed penalty, displacing commentary on exile into the wrong exchange.
The opening misreads Socrates: he rejects choosing known evils over Meletus’s uncertain penalty, rather than refusing any harm he regards as known evil. Placement and listening pass.
Evidence and listening pass, but playback snaps +931: it follows the sons’ rebuke and precedes “If you do this,” so the recap arrives after most of its span.
Accurately orients the return, setting, topic shift, and buildup to Charmides while adding a concise dramatic frame; the opening edge is clean before the source.
Accurate, but it repeats the section's return, setting, Critias, and topic-shift recap. At the edge, nothing precedes it and the same opening source follows.
The summary is accurate and useful, but playback follows “if you actually have it” and precedes “See now whether you have it,” after the anchored close.
The argument is accurate and focused, but playback follows the prior health exchange and precedes “For health, we said,” before its 175b–175e anchor.
Accurately identifies the unresolved aporia, Critias’s behavioral test, and the comic non-closure; it follows the final exchange cleanly and adds a precise closing observation.
The dream and Crito’s appeals are supported, but “the text leaves its meaning at that level” asserts an unsupported absence; the edge falls after “Too clear” before “But, my dear Socrates.”
Accurately presents Crito’s harm-based measure, Socrates’ wisdom-and-folly countermeasure, and their unresolved tension; the edge falls after “That may well be” before “But, Socrates.”
Accurately orients the section's method, expert-opinion analogy, and conditional extension to justice; citations support it, and the pre-46b edge preserves the dramatic transition.
Accurate and well placed between Crito's agreement and Socrates' next question, but it substantially repeats the section's trainer-to-justice explanation and should be differentiated.
The critic's disparagement and reported-speech frame are supported, but the passage does not establish that philosophy becomes a public target; rewrite that overreach.
Fails placement: immediately before is Socrates asking “Whom?” and immediately after is Euthyphro’s answer; this splits a question from its answer.
Evidence and listening pass; placement fails: before the edge Call asks, “you are the man...?”, and after it Socrates begins, “Apparently I can,” splitting question from answer.
The synthesis is clear and well placed after Socrates’ setup and before Hippias’ reply, but “lost his inheritance” exceeds the source’s claim that money was left to and lost by Anaxagoras.
The title calls Laches and Nicias generals without packet support; the body mostly recaps, narrows Socrates’ setting, and overstates his deferral as disclaiming knowledge.
Accurately frames Laches’ skepticism and examples, but the edge follows the preceding question and precedes Lach.’s immediate answer, splitting question from reply.
The summary is accurate and clear, but the edge follows Laches’ question, “What do you mean?”, and precedes Socrates’ immediate answer, splitting question from reply.
“After scrutiny” reverses the source’s sequence: the priest is tested after receiving the lot. The edge follows Clin.’s reply and precedes Ath.’s new sentence, so placement is safe.
Evidence and listening pass, but the edge follows the choir proposal and precedes Ath.'s direct reply; snapping +1268 chars displaces the hinge into the music-official exchange.
Evidence and listening pass, but the edge follows a semicolon after the obedience claim and precedes “Ath. a more complete statement,” splitting the continuing clause.
Evidence supports the catalogue, demand, and prelude; “must address beliefs” is too certain. Placement passes: prior text ends “loosed...”; next begins “Ath. Next...”
Evidence and spoken focus pass, but playback follows the time-limit sentence and precedes Ath.'s forceful-obstruction rule, displacing the section opening into a later exchange.
Evidence and listening pass. Placement splits Socrates’ accusation, “You are deceiving me,” from Hippias’s immediate reply, “Not at all.”
Accurate, concise overview, but remove: the edge falls after Lysis says they stop many things and before Socrates asks “How do you mean?”, splitting prompt and reply.
Evidence and listening pass, but playback follows “so fond I am of my comrades.” and precedes “Accordingly, when I see you and Lysis together,” shifting this section into 212a.
Evidence and listening pass, but the edge follows the 242e conquest sentence and precedes Socrates’ third-war account, displacing commentary on the later 243d-e reversal.
Evidence and listening pass, but playback snaps +1071 chars: before is the proverb's close; after is Socrates beginning a later self-reliance exposition, displacing the section.
The recap is useful and accurately tracks the exchange, but “every bearer” broadens Socrates’ male/female comparisons beyond the cited evidence.
It states as settled that the soul acquired the opinions earlier and is immortal, flattening Socrates’ conditional inference; it follows “Twice” and precedes 85b’s geometry.
Evidence is accurate and concise; the edge falls between Socrates’ question “is it by education?” before and Meno’s immediate answer after, splitting Q/A.
The body accurately frames the later inference, but the edge follows Socrates’ claim that virtue is not teachable and precedes Anytus’ rebuke, displacing the unit’s dramatic setup.
The closing claim that “nothing will be clear” overstates the source’s narrower condition: certainty about how virtue comes requires first defining virtue.
Evidence and listening pass. Playback shifts +1476 chars: before is the shape conclusion at 138a; after begins Ceph.'s exposition that the One cannot be anywhere, displacing the 137c anchor.
Playback falls after 140e: before is the completed age exchange; after is Ceph's 141a time question. This displaces the 140a section overview into a later topic.
The commentary is supported and clear, but the edge follows the One's being/existence exchange and precedes its generation discussion, before the later turn to the Others.

The myth framing supports speculation and epistemic caution, but “consoling picture” is not supported by the cited source or observations. The edge is clean: Socrates’s speech ends before Phaedo’s reply.
The synthesis is accurate and focused, but the edge follows the art-of-speech claim and precedes Socrates’ “wiser masters” reply, before the writing discussion it previews.
Placement splits Socrates’ opening claim before the edge from Protarchus’s immediate “I think I understand you” reply after it; the commentary interrupts that exchange.
The opening and interpretive arc fit the passage, but the cited observation only supports the Alcibiades hunt; claims about Protagoras and the qualified superlative lack accepted support.
Evidence and listening pass. The edge follows the 325e school instruction and precedes Socrates on the masters; +2001 shifts the whole-unit setup into a later exchange, so remove.
Evidence and listening pass, but the edge follows the Stranger’s paid-hunter statement and precedes Theaetetus’s “Yes,” separating a statement from its direct reply.
Evidence and listening pass, but the edge interrupts the Stranger’s opening claim before Theaetetus’s immediate “True,” weakening the exchange’s dramatic continuity.
The interpretation is supported, but placement interrupts after the Stranger's completed correction and before Y. Soc.'s direct reply, splitting prompt from reply.
The edge follows the Stranger’s proposal that the principle applies to all cases and precedes Y. Soc.’s direct “Do so” reply, splitting prompt and reply.
Evidence and listening pass, but the edge follows the Stranger's request to apply weaving and precedes Y. Soc.'s “Very well; let us do so,” splitting prompt and reply.
The commentary accurately isolates shame as the speech's motivational mechanism and civic extrapolation; the pre-speech edge cleanly prepares the coming Phaedrus speech.
Evidence and listening pass; placement fails: the edge follows the army's victory claim and precedes the continued 'For a man in love...' passage, not the mythic turn.
Evidence and listening pass, but the edge falls after the 49e element summary and before Tim's 50a receptacle elaboration, +2840 chars from the section start.

Citations support withholding higher principles, not the claim that Timaeus leaves himself unrestricted; the block also combines epistemic limits with elemental transformation. Placement is clean between 54a paragraphs.
The claims about variety and motion fit the passage, but “account for” overstates the record’s explanatory hypothesis; placement follows 56e’s transformation paragraph and precedes 57a.
Evidence and spoken focus pass, but the edge follows the earth-melting explanation and precedes 61a's earth/water cases, displacing commentary about the later 61c–61d method.
